This file is analytics/Claude-Code-hook-adjacent to the branch's changed claude.plugin.ts / claude-code-otlp-endpoint.ts, so it is flagged for direct review rather than dismissed as environmental; could not confirm from this run alone whether it is a Windows-sandbox artifact (file handle held by a spawned proxy/daemon process preventing cleanup and forwarding) or a real regression.

Self-skip: script printed 'No staged changes to scan' -- validate-secrets.js scans the staged git diff only (by design, to keep gitignored local installs out of pre-commit checks), and nothing was staged in this working tree. Exit 0 is not evidence the branch's diff was scanned. To run it for real locally: 'git add' the changed files (or diff against merge_base) before invoking, with Docker/Podman/Apple-Containers running so the gitleaks image can execute. CI (gitleaks-action@v2 via the secrets-detection reusable workflow) scans the branch diff unconditionally and is the authority this local run could not substitute for.

Checked HEAD~1..HEAD only (the guide's defined range); mirrors but does not substitute for CI's separate pr-title-lint.yml workflow, which lints the PR title itself against the same Conventional Commits config and can only run once a PR exists.

Covered conceptually by the guide's 'secrets' gate above (same Gitleaks tooling), but CI's job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:secrets-detection) calls a remote reusable workflow (codemie-ai/ci-workflows/reusable-secrets-detection.yml) that requires GitHub Actions infra unreachable from this local run.
CodeQL analysis (.github/workflows/codeql.yml) runs via a remote reusable workflow requiring GitHub Advanced Security infra unreachable locally; no local equivalent exists in package.json scripts.
